items.headline: Woman jailed eight months over a dating-app ruse luring victims into rigged mahjong games
items.summary: Olivia Chin Hui Zhen, 31, was sentenced to eight months' jail and fined S$3,000 after pleading guilty to charges including conspiracy to cheat, with 32 further charges taken into consideration.

items.headline: Disruptive passenger escorted off a Singapore-bound Scoot flight, delaying it about two hours
items.summary: A woman was removed from Scoot flight TR905 on 1 October over disruptive behaviour; the flight was delayed roughly two hours and investigations are ongoing.

items.headline: Makeshift stalls openly sell illegal aphrodisiacs along a Geylang pedestrian walkway
items.summary: At least eight makeshift stalls were seen selling illegal sex-enhancement drugs within a roughly 50-metre stretch near the Geylang Road and Aljunied Road junction.

items.headline: IMDA and TikTok launch a programme to build Singapore's short-form 'microdrama' industry
items.summary: The IMDA and TikTok unveiled a six-to-nine-month programme to train local talent in producing short-form microdrama series, with both tracks incorporating AI tools.

items.headline: Boardroom revolt reaches Tata Trusts as members challenge chairman Noel Tata
items.summary: Two Tata Trusts members challenged chairman Noel Tata over a restructuring plan they say he advanced without consulting them; Tata Trusts controls about 66% of Tata Sons.

items.headline: India's finance ministry warns global risks could threaten strong growth and investment
items.summary: The finance ministry cautioned that geopolitical tension, volatile oil prices and trade disruption threaten momentum even after the economy grew about 7.8% in the June quarter.

items.headline: Indian firms face higher borrowing costs as short-term yields jump before the RBI meeting
items.summary: Short-term bond yields surged as the RBI drained excess cash ahead of its 7 October rate decision; the Nifty 50 is in its longest weekly losing streak in nearly 25 years.

items.headline: Congress and a Gen-Z 'Cockroach' movement call nationwide protests demanding the election chief quit
items.summary: The Cockroach Janta Party and Congress called protests from 2 October demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged voter-roll manipulation.

items.headline: UK 30-year borrowing cost hits 6%, its highest since 1998, as debt fears mount
items.summary: Britain's 30-year gilt yield rose to 6.01%, the highest since March 1998, squeezing Chancellor John Healey before his 28 October Budget.

items.headline: Soaring fuel prices hand the chancellor a 4bn pound windfall ahead of the Budget
items.summary: Higher fuel prices are set to give Chancellor John Healey a roughly 4 billion pound tax windfall, intensifying calls to help motorists in his first Budget on 28 October.

items.headline: Labour enjoys a 'Burnham bounce' as polls narrow the gap with Reform UK
items.summary: After Andy Burnham replaced Keir Starmer as PM, a Survation poll put Labour up two points to 29% and Reform UK down one to 23%; Burnham ruled out an early election.

items.headline: Burnham unveils a Water Bill to repeal the Thatcher-era ban on public ownership
items.summary: In his first conference speech as PM, Andy Burnham announced a Water Bill repealing the ban on public ownership of water companies and closing an executive-bonus loophole.

items.headline: Putin rules out a Ukraine ceasefire and warns of 'all weapons' over Kaliningrad
items.summary: At the Valdai forum, Putin ruled out a ceasefire with Ukraine and said Russia would use all the weapons at its disposal if Kaliningrad were attacked.

items.headline: French school and university protests spread, with about 625 detained and 83 officers injured
items.summary: Protests over classroom overcrowding, teacher shortages and budget cuts spread across France, shutting 160+ schools; PM Sebastien Lecornu convened a crisis meeting.

items.headline: Pentagon says the US troop withdrawal from Iraq is complete after a 12-year campaign
items.summary: The Pentagon said the final US and coalition forces made an orderly departure from Erbil Air Base, which had hosted about 1,500 troops, ending the anti-ISIL mission.

items.headline: Gunmen kill seven on a bus in Syria as a pipeline blast knocks three power plants offline
items.summary: Assailants killed at least seven on a bus near Masyaf in Homs province hours after a gas-pipeline explosion near Damascus forced three power plants offline.

items.headline: CNN investigation finds Kushner firm holds a large stake in an Israeli military-linked company
items.summary: A CNN investigation reported that Jared Kushner's private-equity firm holds its largest stake in an Israeli company tied to businesses supporting Israel's military operations.

items.headline: AI voice startup ElevenLabs doubles its valuation to $22 billion in an employee share sale
items.summary: ElevenLabs let staff cash out vested equity at a $22 billion valuation, double its $11 billion February mark, in a $300 million secondary co-led by Wellington and T. Rowe Price.

items.headline: Google releases Gemini 4 Argon, pitched as its most powerful model for cyber defence
items.summary: Alphabet launched Gemini 4 Argon, tuned to autonomously find, validate and patch vulnerabilities and limited to vetted partners through its Fairwind programme.

items.headline: Mandiant founder Kevin Mandia's 'agent swarm' security startup Armadin raises $255m
items.summary: Armadin raised a $255.5 million Series B at a valuation above $2.5 billion, led by Andreessen Horowitz and Accel, to run swarms of AI agents that test enterprise defences.

items.headline: Fervo Energy brings the first enhanced geothermal power to the grid, built in 23 months
items.summary: Fervo began selling power from its Cape Station plant in Utah, the first roughly 33 MW of a planned 100 MW block; the full site could reach 4 GW, with Google contracted for 396 MW.

items.headline: Satlyt raises $8 million to run AI computing workloads directly aboard satellites
items.summary: Satlyt, founded by a former Google and SpaceX product manager, raised an $8 million seed to build software processing AI workloads onboard satellites.

items.headline: S&P 500 edges higher to start October as Treasury yields retreat from multi-year highs
items.summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.19% to 7,666.45 and the Nasdaq added 0.04% to 26,871.60; the 10-year Treasury yield touched about 5.33%, its highest since 2002.

items.headline: Accenture posts its best day ever after an earnings beat and record AI bookings
items.summary: Accenture reported fiscal Q4 earnings of $3.29 a share on revenue of $18.68 billion, both above estimates, with a record 141 bookings of $100 million or more; shares rose about 16%.

items.headline: Nike sales fall 4% as China revenue drops 26% and a restructuring looms
items.summary: Nike reported revenue of $11.21 billion, down 4%, with China sales off 26%; it guided to a high-single-digit fiscal 2027 decline and flagged layoffs, sending shares down about 6%.

items.headline: Oil rises for a third day as Middle East tensions threaten to escalate
items.summary: WTI rose above $93 a barrel and Brent settled near $102 as the Pentagon weighed sending another aircraft carrier and 10,000 personnel to the Gulf amid US-Iran tensions.

items.headline: Global dealmakers chase a $5 trillion M&A record despite a slower third quarter
items.summary: Announced M&A reached $3.8 trillion so far this year and could top 2021's record above $5 trillion, even after Q3 deal value fell about 10% from a year earlier.

items.headline: F1 returns to Sepang for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, its first race there since 2017
items.summary: Formula 1 races at Sepang this weekend for the first time since 2017, with the Bahrain GP relocated after its April cancellation; drivers expect heat and likely rain.

items.headline: Russell says the F1 title pressure is all on Antonelli as Mercedes eye a Sepang upgrade
items.summary: George Russell said Mercedes hope a new upgrade in Malaysia can help him cut Kimi Antonelli's 66-point championship lead, insisting the pressure sits with Antonelli.

items.headline: Djokovic beats Borges for his first win since Wimbledon, improving to 30-0 in Beijing
items.summary: Novak Djokovic beat Nuno Borges 6-3, 7-6(2) in his China Open opener for his first win since the Wimbledon quarter-finals, extending his perfect Beijing record to 30-0.

items.headline: India thrash Sri Lanka by 124 runs to set up an Asian Games gold-medal final with Pakistan
items.summary: India beat Sri Lanka by 124 runs in the Asian Games semi-final, Ishan Kishan making 80 not out off 46, to reach a gold-medal final against Pakistan on 3 October in Japan.

items.headline: NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 makes the fastest crewed US trip to the space station
items.summary: Crew-13 launched from Florida on 1 October with Jessica Watkins, Luke Delaney, Joshua Kutryk and Sergey Teteryatnikov, reaching the ISS in 7 hours 50 minutes.

items.headline: Quantum simulator confirms a 40-year-old physics prediction using trapped atoms
items.summary: A Caltech-led team used neutral-atom quantum simulators of up to 35 atoms to measure energy spectra predicted by conformal field theory, confirming a 40-year-old prediction.

items.headline: Scientists develop a way to watermark AI-designed proteins so labs can trace their origin
items.summary: Researchers unveiled a method to embed invisible watermarks into AI-generated protein sequences and structures without changing function, as a potential biosecurity safeguard.

items.headline: Fossil study finds a dinosaur group evolved flight independently from the birds' line
items.summary: A newly described early-Cretaceous species, Norellraptor barsboldi, suggests microraptorines evolved their own flight apparatus separately from the lineage leading to modern birds.

fun_fact.headline: Sea otters raft together and anchor in kelp while sleeping
fun_fact.body: Sea otters sleep floating on their backs at the surface, and to keep from drifting apart on the current they gather in groups called 'rafts.' They often wrap themselves in strands of kelp, which act as a natural anchor, and have even been seen holding paws so a resting companion does not float away.

puzzle.title: All Labels Lie
puzzle.body: Three boxes are labelled APPLES, ORANGES and BOTH, but every label is wrong. Drawing one fruit from one box, relabel all three correctly.
puzzle.approach: You only need one piece of information; choose where to get it so the all-wrong rule does the rest.
puzzle.answer: Draw from the box labelled BOTH; it must be single-fruit. The fruit you draw names it, then the all-wrong rule forces the other two.

word_puzzle.title: Tall Order
word_puzzle.body: Spelling Bee. Centre letter T; outer letters C A P I O N. Find 4+ letter words containing T; one pangram uses all seven.
word_puzzle.approach: Every word must include the centre letter; hunt for the single word that uses all seven.
word_puzzle.answer: Pangram CAPTION; others include ATTIC, TONIC, TOPIC, PATIO, OPTIC, ANTIC, TITAN, TACIT, ACTION, OPTION, POTION, NOTION, ATTAIN, CAPTAIN.

notes: India ran on fallback sources (Bloomberg, Al Jazeera): all six primary India outlets were unreachable from this environment. UK News ran on fallback sources (Bloomberg, Al Jazeera): BBC and Sky News were unreachable; The Guardian was also unreachable. Singapore ran chiefly on Mothership as CNA, The Straits Times, BBC and Reuters were unreachable; 3 retry attempts were made per blocked section. Global, Tech, Business, Sports and Misc used reachable allowed outlets. Corrected a stale F1 premise carried on 2026-10-01: this weekend's race (Oct 2-4) is the Bahrain Grand Prix held at Sepang, Malaysia, not a Singapore sprint; the Singapore GP is next weekend (Oct 9-11). SGP/ST/CNA, India primary outlets, BBC/Sky and The Guardian were egress-blocked for WebFetch/WebSearch.
